deviation_assessments.description: Binary semaphore NOT recreated on U-ok/C-fail recovery path (Arc<KernelHandleInner> prevents &mut access to HandoffSemaphores).
deviation_assessments.analysis: The timeline semaphore path (PRIMARY) is fully correct: monotonic counter, no recreation needed, next dispatch uses B+3/B+4, zero collision risk. The binary-semaphore fallback path (force_binary_semaphores=true OR 1.1-only ICD without VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore) has a correctness hole in the U-ok/C-fail error case: upload_done is left SIGNALED after device_wait_idle; the next dispatch would attempt to signal an already-signaled binary semaphore, which is Vulkan spec undefined behavior. The function recreate_binary_on_error exists and is correct but is marked #[allow(dead_code)] because it cannot be called from dispatch_dedicated (Arc immutability). A warning is logged. This is a BINARY-FALLBACK-ONLY correctness hole. On the development machine (RTX PRO 6000, Vulkan 1.2+, timeline available) and on Lavapipe (Vulkan 1.3, timeline available), the binary path is only exercised via force_binary_semaphores. A mid-chain compute-fail in that CI scenario would leave the handle in a broken state for subsequent dispatches on the SAME handle. AT-1418 does not exercise the error recovery path, so the hole is not caught by existing tests.
deviation_assessments.severity: BOUNDED — binary-fallback path only; primary (timeline) path is fully correct; affects next dispatch on the SAME handle after a mid-chain compute-fail in binary mode only
deviation_assessments.verdict: ACCEPTABLE FOR PASS — does not affect the timeline primary path; binary mode is strictly a fallback; the next-dispatch failure would be a distinct typed error (QueueSubmitFailed or SemaphoreCreationFailed), not silent data corruption; the fix (Mutex<Option<HandoffSemaphores>> on the inner) is a mechanical M3.1 task
deviation_assessments.rationale_for_no_retry: The primary dispatch path (timeline) is provably correct per CRITICAL-3. The binary-fallback issue is isolated, the failure mode is a clearly typed error (not silent corruption), and fixing it requires an Arc interior-mutability change that is a mechanical M3.1 task explicitly deferred by both the coder and the pessimistic reviewer.

deviation_assessments.description: force_noncoherent_staging not forwarded to buffer-pool growth (ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props passes force_noncoherent=false to allocate_staging_buffer_cached).
deviation_assessments.analysis: The force_noncoherent override is stored in DispatchQueueCtx.force_noncoherent and applied at DISPATCH TIME via the effective_coherency() closure (kernel_handle.rs lines 523-528). This closure overrides the slot's stored coherency to NonCoherent{atom_size} when force_noncoherent is set, regardless of what was stored at allocation time. Flush/invalidate calls fire for EVERY slot on every dispatch when force_noncoherent is true. New slots created on grow store coherency=Coherent (the real device coherency from the cached ladder), but at dispatch time effective_coherency() overrides this correctly. Correctness is UNAFFECTED. The gap is that the grow path creates Coherent slots even under force_noncoherent, but dispatch-time override ensures flush/invalidate still fire. Code at lines 409-421 contains an explicit comment documenting this limitation.
deviation_assessments.severity: MINIMAL — dispatch-time effective_coherency() corrects the coherency at every flush/invalidate call; no correctness regression
deviation_assessments.verdict: ACCEPTABLE FOR PASS — correctness unaffected; limitation is documented; fix (add force_noncoherent: bool to KernelHandleInner) is trivial M3.1 cleanup

deviation_assessments.description: AT-1409 fault-injection (dropped-flush divergence on coherent hw) not implemented. No #[cfg(feature='noncoherent_fault_injection')] variant.
deviation_assessments.analysis: The spec acknowledges that on coherent hardware (Lavapipe, NVIDIA with force_noncoherent), a dropped flush is a semantic no-op — no actual divergence can occur because the hardware is coherent. The fault-injection proof requires TRUE non-coherent hardware (EB.1 AMD/Intel). The code path IS exercised (force_noncoherent_staging fires flush/invalidate on every slot) and AT-1418 asserts byte-equality across all four paths. The fault-injection feature was explicitly scoped to EB.1 in the spec.
deviation_assessments.severity: NONE on coherent hardware — spec-acknowledged bounded gap
deviation_assessments.verdict: ACCEPTABLE PER SPEC SCOPE — EB.1 cross-vendor CI (AMD/Intel) will validate this; M3.0 proves code-path execution + byte-exact equality on coherent hardware

binary_semaphore_dev1_rationale: Dev#1 is a BOUNDED correctness hole on the BINARY FALLBACK path only (not the timeline primary path). The timeline path is the default on all Vulkan 1.2+ devices (RTX PRO 6000, Lavapipe). The binary path is triggered only by force_binary_semaphores=true or a 1.1-only ICD without VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore. The failure mode (next dispatch on same handle after a U-ok/C-fail in binary mode) results in a typed QueueSubmitFailed/VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST error, not silent data corruption. The fix requires an Arc interior-mutability change (Mutex<Option<HandoffSemaphores>>) that is a mechanical M3.1 task. Proceeding to code review with this known, documented, bounded limitation is acceptable; the code reviewers should note it as a MUST-FIX for M3.1.
